Sighnaghi

A small walled town on a ridge above the Alazani Valley, with the most photographed view in Kakheti.

Time needed
3 h
From Tbilisi
110 km · 1:50
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
free

Sighnaghi stands on a ridge some four hundred metres above the floor of the Alazani Valley, and that position is the whole point of the place. From any eastern edge of town the ground drops away and a flat green plain runs out to the wall of the Greater Caucasus — on a clear day the snow line is sharp enough to trace with a finger. The town itself is tiny, well under two thousand residents, and was rebuilt in the mid-2000s with red-tiled roofs, carved wooden balconies and cobbled lanes. Some travellers find the restoration a little too tidy; most simply enjoy it.

The serious monument here is the fortress wall. King Erekle II had it built in the 1770s as a refuge for the surrounding villages during raids from the north-east. Roughly four kilometres of curtain wall survive along with twenty-three towers, which makes it one of the most complete defensive circuits in Georgia. Two sections are open: stairways lead up onto the rampart, and the tower walks give a far better panorama than street level does.

On the main square, the Sighnaghi Museum holds regional archaeology downstairs and a room of Niko Pirosmani canvases upstairs — the painter was born nearby at Mirzaani. Around the square are wine bars and family cellars pouring qvevri wine by the glass, plus the small marriage house that earned the town its "city of love" nickname.

Practical advice

Arrive in the afternoon and stay for sunset — the Alazani view is at its best when the last light hits the Caucasus. Park below the main square or along Chavchavadze Street; the centre is small enough to cross on foot in minutes. Three hours covers the square, the museum and one stretch of wall, but climbing the towers takes longer and the steps are uneven, so wear proper shoes. Cafés, ATMs and toilets are all on or beside the square.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Leave Tbilisi on the Kakheti Highway through Sagarejo and Badiauri, carry on past Tsnori, then take the signed left turn and climb — about 110 km and one hour fifty in total. The surface is asphalt the whole way and an economy car is entirely adequate, though the final ascent is a narrow series of switchbacks. Fuel is easy in Sagarejo, Gurjaani and Tsnori. You can return over the Gombori Pass via Telavi for a more scenic drive; it costs roughly half an hour more and closes in heavy snow.

Nearby places

Monastery

Bodbe Monastery

The burial place of St Nino beside Sighnaghi — one of Kakheti's most visited shrines, with a cypress avenue and valley views.

Nature

Lagodekhi Protected Areas

Georgia's oldest nature reserve on the Azerbaijani border — forest, waterfalls and the multi-day trek to Black Rock Lake.

Winery

Kvareli and the Kindzmarauli zone

Kakheti's main red-wine microzone — tunnel cellars cut into rock, two lakes and a natural base for a harvest trip.
